officialLearningOutcome: describe key features of business models
front: A business model most directly explains — key distinction
back: how a firm creates and delivers value. It connects customers, offerings, channels, pricing, resources, and partners.

officialLearningOutcome: describe key features of business models
front: The “who” in a business model identifies — key distinction
back: customers and customer segments. The who identifies whom the issuer serves.

officialLearningOutcome: describe key features of business models
front: A value proposition describes — key distinction
back: why customers choose the offering. It states the attributes that make customers prefer the offering.

officialLearningOutcome: describe key features of business models
front: The “where” component primarily concerns — key distinction
back: channels used to reach customers. Channels connect the offering with customers.

officialLearningOutcome: describe key features of business models
front: The “how much” component concerns — key distinction
back: pricing. Pricing specifies what customers pay.

officialLearningOutcome: describe key features of business models
front: A value chain is best described as — key distinction
back: internal systems and processes that create customer value. The value chain describes how the firm creates value.

officialLearningOutcome: describe key features of business models
front: A supply chain differs because it includes — key distinction
back: the network inside and outside the firm that produces and delivers. Supply chains can cross organizational boundaries.

officialLearningOutcome: describe key features of business models
front: Customer segmentation groups buyers by — key distinction
back: decision-useful shared attributes. Segmentation supports product, channel, and pricing choices.

officialLearningOutcome: describe key features of business models
front: An analyst should assess a business model by — key distinction
back: developing an independent understanding. Independent analysis reveals prospects, dependencies, and risks.

officialLearningOutcome: describe key features of business models
front: Pricing power is strongest when — key distinction
back: differentiation is meaningful and alternatives are limited. Differentiation and limited alternatives support pricing power.

officialLearningOutcome: describe key features of business models
front: An asset-light operating model generally — key distinction
back: relies less on owned physical assets. Asset-light describes resource configuration, not absence of risk.

officialLearningOutcome: describe key features of business models
front: Scalability means the firm can — key distinction
back: grow output or users without proportional resource growth. Scalability concerns how costs and capacity behave as activity expands.

officialLearningOutcome: describe key features of business models
front: Customer concentration creates risk because — key distinction
back: loss of a major buyer can materially reduce activity. Reliance on few buyers raises exposure to individual relationships.

officialLearningOutcome: describe key features of business models
front: Recurring revenue generally improves — key distinction
back: visibility and customer-lifetime continuity. Recurring arrangements can make revenue more predictable but do not guarantee retention.

officialLearningOutcome: describe key features of business models
front: Unit economics are used to examine — key distinction
back: economics at the customer or transaction level. They test whether incremental activity creates attractive economics.

officialLearningOutcome: describe key features of business models
front: The economic balance sheet broadens analysis to — key distinction
back: valuable relationships and capabilities not fully reported. Business-model analysis includes resources and relationships beyond reported statements.

officialLearningOutcome: describe key features of business models
front: A channel conflict can arise when — key distinction
back: direct and intermediary routes compete for the same customers. Overlapping routes can create partner tension and inconsistent pricing.

officialLearningOutcome: describe key features of business models
front: A sound qualitative review links — key distinction
back: strategy, operations, markets, partners, risks, and financial profile. Business-model analysis integrates how the issuer actually works.

officialLearningOutcome: describe key features of business models
front: A model with high fixed costs and low marginal costs may be — key distinction
back: highly scalable after sufficient volume. Incremental growth can be inexpensive once fixed infrastructure exists.

officialLearningOutcome: describe key features of business models
front: A key-partner dependency is most concerning when — key distinction
back: the input is critical and switching alternatives are scarce. Critical scarce partners create operating vulnerability.

officialLearningOutcome: describe key features of business models
front: A value proposition is weak when — key distinction
back: customers see little meaningful difference from alternatives. Weak differentiation limits willingness to choose or pay.

officialLearningOutcome: describe key features of business models
front: A coherent model requires pricing to — key distinction
back: fit the value proposition and delivery cost. Price must align with customer value and the economics of delivery.

officialLearningOutcome: describe key features of business models
front: Business-model risk analysis should test — key distinction
back: whether components reinforce or contradict each other. Internal consistency is central to qualitative analysis.

officialLearningOutcome: describe various types of business models
front: A subscription model earns revenue primarily through — key distinction
back: recurring access fees. Subscriptions charge periodically for continued access.

officialLearningOutcome: describe various types of business models
front: A transaction-fee model earns revenue when — key distinction
back: a facilitated exchange occurs. Fees are tied to completed transactions.

officialLearningOutcome: describe various types of business models
front: An advertising model primarily monetizes — key distinction
back: audience attention or access. Advertisers pay to reach an audience.

officialLearningOutcome: describe various types of business models
front: A licensing model permits another party to use — key distinction
back: intellectual property or a brand for compensation. Licensing monetizes rights, often through royalties.

officialLearningOutcome: describe various types of business models
front: A franchise model combines — key distinction
back: a proven format and brand with independently operated outlets. Franchisees operate under the franchisor’s system and brand.

officialLearningOutcome: describe various types of business models
front: A contract manufacturer primarily — key distinction
back: produces goods marketed by another firm. The customer owns the market-facing product or brand.

officialLearningOutcome: describe various types of business models
front: Crowdsourcing relies on — key distinction
back: users contributing content, ideas, or work. User contribution is the defining mechanism.

officialLearningOutcome: describe various types of business models
front: A platform model commonly creates value by — key distinction
back: enabling interactions among participant groups. Platforms coordinate participants and may benefit from network effects.

officialLearningOutcome: describe various types of business models
front: A marketplace typically monetizes — key distinction
back: matching buyers and sellers, often for a fee. Marketplaces facilitate exchange.

officialLearningOutcome: describe various types of business models
front: Freemium pricing uses — key distinction
back: a free basic tier and paid enhanced access. Free entry supports adoption while premium features monetize some users.

officialLearningOutcome: describe various types of business models
front: Penetration pricing deliberately uses — key distinction
back: low initial prices to build scale or share. The firm sacrifices initial margin to accelerate adoption.

officialLearningOutcome: describe various types of business models
front: Premium pricing is most consistent with — key distinction
back: strong differentiation and perceived superior value. Customers pay more for valued attributes or positioning.

officialLearningOutcome: describe various types of business models
front: Tiered pricing varies price by — key distinction
back: volume, features, or service level. Tiers segment willingness to pay or usage.

officialLearningOutcome: describe various types of business models
front: Dynamic pricing changes with — key distinction
back: conditions such as demand, capacity, or time. Dynamic prices respond to changing conditions.

officialLearningOutcome: describe various types of business models
front: Bundling means — key distinction
back: selling multiple products or services together. A bundle combines offerings in one package or required set.

officialLearningOutcome: describe various types of business models
front: A razor-and-razorblade model pairs — key distinction
back: a low-priced durable item with higher-margin consumables. The installed base drives repeat consumable purchases.

officialLearningOutcome: describe various types of business models
front: An add-on model earns margin from — key distinction
back: optional features, customization, or extra content. The core purchase is supplemented by paid extras.

officialLearningOutcome: describe various types of business models
front: An auction model determines price through — key distinction
back: competitive bidding. Bids establish the transaction price.

officialLearningOutcome: describe various types of business models
front: An omnichannel strategy seeks to — key distinction
back: coordinate physical and digital customer routes. Customers interact across integrated channels.

officialLearningOutcome: describe various types of business models
front: A direct-sales model is distinguished by — key distinction
back: selling to customers without a traditional reseller chain. The producer controls the customer transaction directly.

officialLearningOutcome: describe various types of business models
front: A reseller model creates value by — key distinction
back: distributing or augmenting another producer’s offering. Resellers connect upstream products to downstream customers.

officialLearningOutcome: describe various types of business models
front: A model combining subscriptions and transaction fees should be analyzed as — key distinction
back: a hybrid with multiple revenue mechanisms. Real issuers often combine conventional mechanisms.
